en.greeting: Hi! Today you're the bridge again, but with bigger messages: a phone call for a colleague who is out, or a long Indonesian announcement in the office group. You'll pass them on in short, clear English. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Who called, then the message
steps.text: Your colleague Tom is out. The phone rings: it's Sari, with a message for him. How do you tell Tom later?
steps.body:
A good message has three parts:
- **Who + what they did**, in the past, because the call is finished: *Sari **called**.* (not *Sari call*)
- **The message**, in 1–3 short sentences: *She can't come today. She's sick.*
- **What they want**: *Please call her back.*
Indonesian shows the past only with *tadi* or *kemarin*; English changes the verb: call → **called**, come → **came**.

steps.title: Whole messages
steps.text: Here are some messages, first in Indonesian, then passed on in English.
steps.body: Short sentences, one fact each. **texted** sounds like 'TEK-stid'.

examples.en: Sari called. She can't come today. She's sick.
examples.id: Sari: 'Saya tidak bisa datang hari ini. Saya sakit.'

examples.en: Budi texted. He missed the bus. He's late.
examples.id: Budi: 'Saya ketinggalan bus. Saya terlambat.'

examples.en: Pak Hasan came at two. He had a question about the report.
examples.id: Pak Hasan datang jam 2. Dia mau tanya soal laporan.

examples.en: Bu Ani called. Please call her back.
examples.id: Bu Ani: 'Tolong telepon saya kembali.'

steps.title: I becomes he or she
steps.text: Did you notice? Sari said 'saya', but you said 'she'. Here's why.
steps.body:
The message is in the sender's words. You talk **about** the sender, so: **I → he/she**, **my → his/her**, **me → him/her**, **we → they**. But if the message is **for** your listener, **you** stays you: Pak Hasan to Tom, *'Saya tunggu Bapak di lobi'* → *He's waiting for you.*
Trap: Indonesian *dia* and *-nya* are the same for a man and a woman. English must choose: look at who sent it.

pairs.id: Bapak / Ibu / kamu (untuk pendengarmu) → tetap you

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pak Rudi phones the office. Tom is out, so you take the message.

question.prompt: Pak Rudi says: 'Saya tidak bisa datang besok. Istri saya sakit.' Which message do you give Tom?
options: Pak Rudi called. I can't come tomorrow. My wife is sick.
Pak Rudi called. He can't come tomorrow. Her wife is sick.
Pak Rudi called. He can't come tomorrow. His wife is sick.
question.explanation: Pak Rudi is a man, so *saya* becomes **he**, and *istri saya* (the owner) becomes **his** wife. *I* and *my* would mean you; *her* is for a woman owner (the *-nya* trap).

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Now Budi texts from the station. Pass it on to Tom.

question.prompt: Budi texts: 'Kereta saya terlambat 30 menit.' Arrange the words for Tom.
question.solution: His train is thirty minutes late.
question.explanation: The message is from Budi, a man, so *kereta saya* becomes **his train**. Then **is** (Indonesian has no 'to be') and the time: **thirty minutes late**.

steps.title: Notices: only the key facts
steps.text: Now the second skill. The office group posts a long announcement in Indonesian, and Emma asks: what does it say?
steps.body:
Don't translate every word. Skip the polite parts (*Dengan hormat, diberitahukan kepada…, Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih*). Ask: **What?** **When?** **Where?** (and sometimes **What do I do?**). Then say it in one or two short sentences.
Watch the word-for-word traps: **air mati** = *There's no water* (not 'the water is dead'), **sekolah libur** = *There's no school*. You can use the present for tomorrow: *The office **is** closed tomorrow.*

pairs.en: The meeting is now on Wednesday.

steps.title: From notice to English
steps.text: Long Indonesian on the right, the short English summary on the left.
steps.body: Each summary keeps only what, when and where.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A message arrives in the office group. Emma asks you about it.

question.prompt: The group says: 'Selamat siang Bapak/Ibu. Rapat bulanan hari ini pindah ke ruang 5, jam tetap 15.00. Terima kasih 🙏' What do you tell Emma?
options: The monthly meeting today is in room 5 at three p.m.
The monthly meeting today is in room 3 at five p.m.
question.explanation: The key facts: what (the monthly meeting), where (room **5**) and when (15.00 − 12 = **three p.m.**; *jam tetap* means the time doesn't change). The last option mixes up the 5 and the 15.00; the meeting is not cancelled.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Tom lives in your neighbourhood. The RT group sends a message.

question.prompt: The RT group says: 'Info warga: kerja bakti hari Minggu jam 07.00, kumpul di depan masjid. Bawa sapu ya!' What do you tell Tom?
options: The clean-up is on Sunday at seven a.m., in front of the mosque. Bring a broom.
The clean-up is on Sunday at seven p.m., in the mosque. Bring a broom.
The clean-up is on Monday at seven a.m., in front of the mosque. Buy a broom.
question.explanation: What: a community clean-up. When: **Sunday** (Minggu), 07.00 = **seven a.m.** Where: **in front of** (di depan) the mosque. What to do: **bring** (bawa) a broom. Each wrong option changes one key fact.

steps.title: Listen and read
steps.text: Want more practice? Listen to someone leaving a phone message, and read a real-style notice to find the key facts.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu jadi jembatan lagi, tapi dengan pesan yang lebih panjang: telepon untuk rekan kerja yang sedang keluar, atau pengumuman panjang berbahasa Indonesia di grup kantor. Kamu akan meneruskannya dalam bahasa Inggris yang pendek dan jelas. Yuk, langkah demi langkah.

steps.title: Siapa yang menelepon, lalu pesannya
steps.text: Rekan kerjamu Tom sedang keluar. Telepon berdering: Sari, dengan pesan untuknya. Bagaimana kamu menyampaikannya ke Tom nanti?
steps.body:
Pesan yang baik punya tiga bagian:
- **Siapa + apa yang dia lakukan**, dalam bentuk lampau, karena teleponnya sudah selesai: *Sari **called**.* (bukan *Sari call*)
- **Isi pesannya**, dalam 1–3 kalimat pendek: *She can't come today. She's sick.*
- **Apa yang dia minta**: *Please call her back.*
Bahasa Indonesia menunjukkan lampau hanya dengan *tadi* atau *kemarin*; bahasa Inggris mengubah kata kerjanya: call → **called**, come → **came**.

steps.title: Pesan utuh
steps.text: Ini beberapa pesan, pertama dalam bahasa Indonesia, lalu diteruskan dalam bahasa Inggris.
steps.body: Kalimat pendek, satu info per kalimat. **texted** dibaca 'TEK-stid'.

examples.en: Sari called. She can't come today. She's sick.
examples.id: Sari: 'Saya tidak bisa datang hari ini. Saya sakit.'

examples.en: Budi texted. He missed the bus. He's late.
examples.id: Budi: 'Saya ketinggalan bus. Saya terlambat.'

examples.en: Pak Hasan came at two. He had a question about the report.
examples.id: Pak Hasan datang jam 2. Dia mau tanya soal laporan.

examples.en: Bu Ani called. Please call her back.
examples.id: Bu Ani: 'Tolong telepon saya kembali.'

steps.title: I berubah jadi he atau she
steps.text: Kamu perhatikan? Sari bilang 'saya', tapi kamu bilang 'she'. Ini alasannya.
steps.body:
Pesan itu memakai kata-kata pengirimnya. Kamu bicara **tentang** pengirimnya, jadi: **I → he/she**, **my → his/her**, **me → him/her**, **we → they**. Tapi kalau pesannya **untuk** pendengarmu, **you** tetap you: Pak Hasan ke Tom, *'Saya tunggu Bapak di lobi'* → *He's waiting for you.*
Jebakan: *dia* dan *-nya* sama untuk laki-laki dan perempuan. Bahasa Inggris harus memilih: lihat siapa pengirimnya.

pairs.id: Bapak / Ibu / kamu (untuk pendengarmu) → tetap you

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pak Rudi menelepon kantor. Tom sedang keluar, jadi kamu yang mencatat pesannya.

question.prompt: Pak Rudi bilang: 'Saya tidak bisa datang besok. Istri saya sakit.' Pesan mana yang kamu sampaikan ke Tom?
options: Pak Rudi called. I can't come tomorrow. My wife is sick.
Pak Rudi called. He can't come tomorrow. Her wife is sick.
Pak Rudi called. He can't come tomorrow. His wife is sick.
question.explanation: Pak Rudi laki-laki, jadi *saya* berubah jadi **he**, dan *istri saya* (pemilik) jadi **his** wife. *I* dan *my* berarti kamu sendiri; *her* untuk pemilik perempuan (jebakan *-nya*).

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sekarang Budi kirim pesan dari stasiun. Teruskan ke Tom.

question.prompt: Budi kirim pesan: 'Kereta saya terlambat 30 menit.' Susun kata-katanya untuk Tom.
question.solution: His train is thirty minutes late.
question.explanation: Pesannya dari Budi, laki-laki, jadi *kereta saya* berubah jadi **his train**. Lalu **is** (bahasa Indonesia tidak punya 'to be') dan waktunya: **thirty minutes late**.

steps.title: Pengumuman: info pentingnya saja
steps.text: Sekarang keterampilan kedua. Grup kantor mengirim pengumuman panjang berbahasa Indonesia, dan Emma bertanya: isinya apa?
steps.body:
Jangan terjemahkan setiap kata. Lewati bagian yang sopan (*Dengan hormat, diberitahukan kepada…, Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih*). Tanyakan: **What?** (apa) **When?** (kapan) **Where?** (di mana), dan kadang **What do I do?** Lalu sampaikan dalam satu atau dua kalimat pendek.
Hati-hati jebakan kata per kata: **air mati** = *There's no water* (bukan 'the water is dead'), **sekolah libur** = *There's no school*. Untuk besok boleh pakai present: *The office **is** closed tomorrow.*

pairs.en: The meeting is now on Wednesday.

steps.title: Dari pengumuman ke bahasa Inggris
steps.text: Bahasa Indonesia yang panjang di kanan, ringkasan bahasa Inggris yang pendek di kiri.
steps.body: Setiap ringkasan hanya menyimpan apa, kapan dan di mana.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Ada pesan masuk di grup kantor. Emma bertanya padamu.

question.prompt: Grupnya menulis: 'Selamat siang Bapak/Ibu. Rapat bulanan hari ini pindah ke ruang 5, jam tetap 15.00. Terima kasih 🙏' Apa yang kamu sampaikan ke Emma?
options: The monthly meeting today is in room 5 at three p.m.
The monthly meeting today is in room 3 at five p.m.
question.explanation: Info pentingnya: apa (rapat bulanan), di mana (ruang **5**) dan kapan (15.00 − 12 = **three p.m.**; *jam tetap* artinya jamnya tidak berubah). Pilihan terakhir mencampur angka 5 dan 15.00; rapatnya juga tidak dibatalkan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Tom tinggal di lingkunganmu. Grup RT mengirim pesan.

question.prompt: Grup RT menulis: 'Info warga: kerja bakti hari Minggu jam 07.00, kumpul di depan masjid. Bawa sapu ya!' Apa yang kamu sampaikan ke Tom?
options: The clean-up is on Sunday at seven a.m., in front of the mosque. Bring a broom.
The clean-up is on Sunday at seven p.m., in the mosque. Bring a broom.
The clean-up is on Monday at seven a.m., in front of the mosque. Buy a broom.
question.explanation: Apa: kerja bakti (a community clean-up). Kapan: **Sunday** (Minggu), 07.00 = **seven a.m.** Di mana: **in front of** (di depan) masjid. Yang harus dilakukan: **bring** (bawa) sapu (a broom). Setiap pilihan yang salah mengubah satu info penting.
